Lemma
[a velocity-seeded parallel orthonormal frame along a geodesic]

1. ch9:3.1Let $\gamma :[a,b] o M$ be a geodesic with $\gamma '(a) e 0$. Then there are parallel fields $e_1,\dots ,e_n$ along $\gamma $, orthonormal at every $t\in [a,b]$, and a distinguished index $n_0$ with $e_{n_0}(t)=\ell ^{-1}\gamma '(t)$ for all $t$, where $\ell =|\gamma '|>0$ is the (constant) speed. In particular $e_i(t)\perp \gamma '(t)$ for $i e n_0$.
Proof

\sketch Extend the unit velocity $\ell ^{-1}\gamma '(a)$ to a $g$-orthonormal basis of $T_{\gamma (a)}M$ and parallel-transport it along $\gamma $; parallel transport is a linear isometry, so the frame stays orthonormal. The distinguished transported member and $\ell ^{-1}\gamma '$ are both parallel fields with the same value at $a$, so by uniqueness of parallel transport they agree on $[a,b]$.
